core_obligations: Final object and Hausdorffness (proof lines 7482-7489): the singleton space is final, and for morphisms X -> Z and Y -> Z the fibre product is a subspace of X x Y, hence Hausdorff because the product is.
Quasi-compact case (proof lines 7490-7497): if X and Y are quasi-compact then so is X x Y by Tychonoff, and the fibre product is a closed subspace of it, hence quasi-compact.

General case (proof lines 7498-7503): for arbitrary points x and y one chooses quasi-compact neighbourhoods E and F; the preceding step makes E x_Z F a quasi-compact neighbourhood of (x, y), so the fibre product is locally quasi-compact Hausdorff, hence an object of the category.
proof_roadmap: Identify the final object and the Hausdorff property of the fibre product.
Use Tychonoff and closedness to get quasi-compactness of fibre products of quasi-compact objects.
Produce quasi-compact neighbourhoods at an arbitrary point to conclude membership in the category.
difficulty_reason: The lemma verifies the categorical and quasi-compactness properties of the category LC of locally quasi-compact Hausdorff spaces (statement lines 7473-7479). The proof (proof lines 7481-7503) uses that the fibre product is a subspace of the product for Hausdorffness, Tychonoff together with closedness for quasi-compactness, and a two-neighbourhood argument for the general case. H2: three short topological steps, written out.
